indicators.title: Grain in storage
indicators.question: Is there more or less grain in the country's elevators and ports than usual for this time of year?
indicators.definition: Wheat, canola and other grains held in licensed grain elevators across the Prairies and at port terminals, as reported each week by the Canadian Grain Commission.
indicators.how_calculated: We add up all grain in storage at the end of the latest week and compare the total with the same week in each of the past five crop years.
indicators.does_not_show: Grain still on farms, which is most of Canada's grain, and food further along the chain. A high number can mean a comfortable reserve, or grain that cannot move. Read it alongside grain shipped through ports.

headline.text: Grain elevators and port terminals held 7.25 million tonnes of grain in the week ending 4 October 2026. That is higher than at this time of year in any of the past five years. It is about 2% above the typical level. Worth watching. One unusual reading does not mean a crisis.

indicators.baseline_rule: Compared with the same week in each of the past 5 crop years (at least 3 needed). A crop year runs from August to July.

indicators.title: Grain shipped through ports
indicators.question: Is grain leaving Canada's ports at a normal pace?
indicators.definition: Grain and oilseeds shipped abroad from port terminals in Vancouver, Prince Rupert, Thunder Bay, the St. Lawrence and elsewhere, reported each week by the Canadian Grain Commission.
indicators.how_calculated: We add up the latest four weeks, because ships arrive unevenly, and compare the total with the same four weeks in each of the past five crop years.
indicators.does_not_show: Why the pace changed. A slowdown can come from rail or port problems, weather, a smaller harvest or weaker sales. Grain sent to the United States by rail or truck is not included.

headline.text: Ports shipped 3.21 million tonnes of grain abroad in the four weeks to 4 October 2026. That is normal for this time of year: it is within the range of the past five years. It is about 4% above the typical level.

indicators.baseline_rule: Compared with the same week in each of the past 5 crop years (at least 3 needed). A crop year runs from August to July.

indicators.title: Fresh fruit and vegetable prices
indicators.question: Are fresh fruit and vegetable prices unusual for this time of year?
indicators.unit: Canadian dollars per box or bag
indicators.definition: Daily wholesale prices at the Toronto wholesale market for 12 fruits and vegetables, from Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada. Each product is always the same variety, grade, origin and box size, so its price can be compared over time.
indicators.how_calculated: For each product we take the average price in the latest week and compare it with the same week in up to 5 past years. Past prices are first converted to October 2026's dollars using the Consumer Price Index, so inflation alone does not make today's prices look high. A product is flagged only if this week's price is above or below every past year.
indicators.does_not_show: What shoppers pay in stores, prices in other cities, or why a price changed. Weather where the food is grown, the exchange rate, quality and the timing of harvests all move wholesale prices.

headline.text: We follow 12 fresh fruits and vegetables at the Toronto wholesale market. In the latest week, two cost more and two cost less than at this time of year in any recent year, after allowing for inflation. Four are in their normal range, and for four we do not have enough past data.

indicators.baseline_rule: Compared with the same week in up to 5 past years, in today's dollars (at least 3 years needed).

indicators.title: Grocery prices compared with wages
indicators.question: Are grocery prices rising faster than what people earn?
indicators.definition: How much grocery prices changed over 12 months (Statistics Canada's Consumer Price Index for food bought in stores), set against how much the average hourly wage changed over the same 12 months (Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey).
indicators.how_calculated: For each month we compare prices and wages with the same month a year earlier. The gap is the difference between the two changes, in percentage points.
indicators.does_not_show: Who is struggling. National averages hide people without wages, such as pensioners and people on income support, differences between regions, and households that spend a larger share of their income on food.

headline.text: In October 2026, grocery prices were 2.0% higher than a year earlier, and average hourly wages were 2.2% higher. Wages have risen faster than grocery prices for two months in a row.

indicators.baseline_rule: Compared with the same month one year earlier.

indicators.title: Food recalls
indicators.question: Is the Canadian Food Inspection Agency recalling more food than usual?
indicators.definition: Food recall and safety notices from the Canadian Food Inspection Agency, published on the Government of Canada's recalls website.
indicators.how_calculated: We count notices in the latest 30 days and compare the count with the same 30 days in each of the past 5 years.
indicators.does_not_show: How much food was affected. Most recalls cover one brand or one batch and do not affect supply. The data give the date a notice was last updated, not first issued, so counts are approximate.

headline.text: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency issued 19 food recall notices in the 30 days to 18 November 2026. That is normal for this time of year: it is within the range of the past five years. It is about 21% below the typical level.

indicators.baseline_rule: Compared with the same 30 days in each of the past 5 years.

indicators.title: Weather warnings
indicators.question: Which weather warnings are in effect, and where?
indicators.definition: Warnings, watches, advisories and special statements from Environment and Climate Change Canada. Alerts of the same type issued at the same time in one province count once.
indicators.how_calculated: We count alerts that have not yet expired. The map on the overview page also checks Environment and Climate Change Canada's service directly each time you open it.
indicators.does_not_show: Whether farms, livestock or transport are actually affected. Alert areas are forecast regions, not farmland.

headline.text: 11 weather alerts were in effect in four provinces or territories when we last checked, including five warnings.
